chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I was sitting with a judge from the judges of Medina when two men came to him. One of them said, "I hired this one to take me to the market on such and such a day, and he did not do it." The judge said, "There is no fee for him." I said: "So I called him and said, "O servant of Allah, it is not for you to go away with his right." And I said to the other, "It is not for you to take everything that is upon him. Reconcile, so that you return (some fees) between you two."'

key_terms.تَكَارَيْتُ: I hired / I agreed on a wage
key_terms.يُوَافِي بِيَ: He meets me / takes me to

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on compensation when a hired service is not fully rendered?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *sulh* (amicable settlement) in commercial disputes, advising mutual concession rather than rigid legalism. This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving social harmony and fairness in contracts, where both parties share the loss or gain to avoid injustice. It serves as a practical guide for resolving disagreements in hiring and services through compromise rather than strict adjudication.
